why can't append the log in the above line itself ?
can we say "Failed to validate primary EEPROM {PATH} against its redundant EEPROM." ?
Since ValidateRedundantEEPROM takes an EEPROM path as input, should we enforce the -H option as mandatory from the user as well? Just a thought .

The --validateRedundantEeprom operation is unambiguous and it only works with EEPROM paths. Unlike read/write operations that can target either Dbus or hardware, this validation always operates on physical EEPROMs.
is it "Validate primary EEPROM against its redundant EEPROM" ?
should the EEPROM path validation be moved into validateRedundantEeprom()? This would keep main() cleaner and encapsulate the validation within the API.
Acknowledged , Moved the eeprom path validation from main() .
"Failed to check if EEPROM path exists, reason:" ?
should this api part to tool_utils ?
moved dbus call for validateredundanteeprom to utils file .
do we need this check, will manager method take care of it ?
Suggestion: use C++23 approach `std::println(std::stderr,<formatted string>);` avoids intermediate string memory allocations

input can itself a redundant path, so avoid saying primary path.
same for below as well.
Suggestion: use C++23 approach `std::println(std::stdcout,<formatted string>);` avoids intermediate string memory allocations
input can itself a redundant path, so avoid saying primary path.
Do we need a call in the API name ?
as this is c++23 feature, specifying version as c++23 in meson explicitly would be better.
The root meson.build already sets: 'cpp_std=c++23'.This applies in the entire project, including subdirectories.
description also contains same wordings, can we have shorter title "Validate EEPROM" instead ?

1. should we shorten the option, which is easier to write as well, like --validate.

2. -v generally used for verbose or version option, if vpd-tool wants to implement verbose later and generically used flag(-v) won't be available.
Hence should we consider using other letter for this flag ?

--validate is too generic instead --validateRedundantEeprom is self-documenting and immediately clear . --validate would be ambiguous to user it does not explain (validate what?). 
And for shorter and quick option we have '-e' (updated from '-v')
Do we need this extra variable if it is being used just at one place? Use the API in place?
